sections.heading: The Role
sections.content: I led the development and implementation of group-wide innovation management systems at Gerresheimer, building frameworks for innovation strategy, processes, and culture change across the organisation. My work focused on enabling cross-divisional collaboration, providing strategic guidance to innovation projects, and establishing measurement systems to ensure alignment with business objectives.

sections.heading: Accessible Innovation
sections.content: Expanded beyond product innovation to serve Key Account Management, Connected Packaging, Medical & Patient Affairs, and IP departments. Leaders started calling me when they only had rough ideas, which meant we'd built trust.

sections.heading: Connecting Expertise
sections.content:
Organised Gerresheimer's first global hackathon. 90 idea submissions, 30 participants from 15 locations, 5 follow-up projects funded.

More importantly: teams discovered they were solving the same problems in parallel. Some participants later joined the global talent program.

sections.heading: Structuring Ambiguity
sections.content:
Took the existing innovation funnel and gave it clear time boundaries (max 6 months, then re-evaluate).

Designed and facilitated 10+ problem-exploration sessions that turned into funded projects.

sections.heading: The insight
sections.content:
The work isn't innovation itself—it's creating the conditions where innovation becomes possible.
That means: 

* Building trust with compliance teams, not working around them
* Designing processes that feel safe for risk-averse engineers
* Making innovation visible and measurable for executives
* Connecting disconnected teams across a global organization

quote.text: "Innovation in a regulated industry isn't about moving fast and breaking things. It's about creating safe spaces for experimentation within a system designed to prevent change."

sections.heading: What I'd do differently
sections.content: I treated compliance as an obstacle to work around instead of a partner to bring in early. Meant I designed two programs that got killed in review because they didn't account for documentation requirements. Expensive lesson. Now I start every project with a coffee chat with the compliance team—not to ask permission, but to understand their constraints before I'm too invested in a specific approach.

preview.title: Built innovation infrastructure from zero in a 150-year-old company
